page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.large is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and driven by custom 64-bit ARM-based AWS Graviton2 processors featuring Neoverse-N1 cores running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, providing direct hardware execution on both vCPUs. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, delivering a high 1:16 core-to-memory ratio with 16.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware provisioning also includes a bundled 118 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume and a 1 Gbps baseline network interconnect.

Benchmark results highlight an operational profile prioritizing memory capacity over raw computational throughput. The instance recorded a stress-ng single-core score of 1519.29 and a multi-core score of 3013.58, alongside a Geekbench multi-core rating of 1725.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 1349.53. Memory throughput yields 36.51 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 17.89 GB/sec for uncached writes. Redis SET benchmarks yielded 2.32 million operations per second. The primary hardware tradeoff is lower multi-threaded computational speed in exchange for substantial memory volume per core.

From an infrastructure perspective, the high RAM density relative to compute allocation provides strong cost efficiency for environments constrained by memory footprint rather than CPU cycles. The x2gd.large is suited for memory-intensive workloads that require low-latency access to sizable datasets, such as Redis and Memcached caching tiers, small in-memory relational databases, real-time analytics aggregation, and memory-bound background queues.
